A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CABLE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling perplexities, BERT retrieval scores, runtime and memory measurements, ablations, and training-loss curves.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds DAPEv2 augmentation comparisons and visual analyses of learned positional biases.

M1.justification: Core CABLE equations, CABLE NW, and K-CABLE remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds an evaluated DAPEv2+CABLE variant incorporating DAPEv2's convolutional processing of the attention matrix, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage remains the same: FineWeb-Edu/FineWeb and WikiText language modeling, plus MS-MARCO training and English MLDR retrieval. The new comparisons and visualizations use existing coverage; the shorter training context changes settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 introduces DAPEv2+CABLE and DAPEv2+Kerple alongside unaugmented CABLE and Kerple, extending evaluation to a directly relevant data-dependent competitor family absent from v2. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain intact. CoPE and FoX are discussed but not quantitatively evaluated.

E3.justification: The added DAPEv2 comparison uses GPT-2 Small trained at sequence length 512 and evaluated from 512 to 8192, distinct from the retained length-1024 training experiments. The new visualization analysis examines a randomly selected 512-token example in the final layer. Existing benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix A.3 add a single-example qualitative analysis of context and head dependence through bias and attention maps. Section 5.3 also examines augmentation effects with and without DAPEv2. Existing CABLE NW and kernelized-CABLE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds or reports confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All retained benchmark tables have identical values, but v3 adds substantive accuracy and efficiency findings. At length 8192, new Table 2 reports perplexities of 19.87, 39.38, 18.63, and 18.92 for CABLE, Kerple, DAPEv2+CABLE, and DAPEv2+Kerple respectively. Section 5.3 reports training throughput falling from 1.9M to 0.6M tokens/sec with CABLE augmentation and 1.7-fold slower inference. These are new comparisons under length-512 training, not improvements over v2's length-1024 experiments.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the ALiBi special-case argument, and the K-CABLE kernel are unchanged. Identifying FIRE's existing function as an MLP adds explanation without changing mathematical reasoning. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain their central claims. The conclusion removes the specific assertion that CABLE trained at length 1024 outperforms a sinusoidal model trained and tested at length 8192, narrowing a subsidiary claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds a proposed explanation involving weaker penalties for anchor tokens and stronger penalties for less informative tokens, alongside an accuracy–efficiency interpretation of DAPEv2 augmentation. It removes the FIRE-specific explanation of underperformance. The limitations discussion remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 3 now identifies GPT-2 Medium, while the new comparison and visualization sections disclose tensor shapes and final-layer/example-selection details. The advertised code destination changes from axiomlab/cable to AlgonetLabs/Cable. v2's sequential-generation timing explanation is removed, although the caption retains batched versus unbatched information.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces its blanket characterization of existing additive biases as static with explicit positioning against CoPE, DAPE/DAPEv2, and FoX. It distinguishes continuous biases, standalone operation, computational cost, and query-conditioned slopes. CoPE and two DAPE references are added; Csordás, Dong, Qin, and Song–Zhong references disappear with the shortened overview.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the related-work opening and conclusion, revises the results roadmap, and moves bidirectional-model results after the new comparison and analysis sections. Model naming is standardized toward GPT-2, affiliation text changes, and an equal-contribution note is added. Most existing prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a comparison table, a four-panel bias figure, and eight appendix figures showing headwise biases or attention scores. This substantially expands the visual evidence beyond the existing plots and schematic. Earlier figures and tables remain, with relocation, renumbering, and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: The DAPEv2 comparison addresses a missing comparison with closely related work and documents its accuracy–efficiency tradeoff. Bias visualizations improve inspectability, and v3 removes the 1024-versus-8192 conclusion claim for which v2 supplies no matching experiment. These are useful but limited gains: existing benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the new semantic interpretation rests on one unannotated example without direct validation.
